title: Greek mill
prompt: A labelled teaching model of the Greek mill waterwheel diagram on page 32 shows only a chute feeding a horizontal paddle rotor and its direct vertical axle, with a water supply and catch tray as bench fixtures. Open water turns the rotor and axle. Reduce flow changes the water input. Slow view slows only the explanatory animation so the water path and shaft rotation can be followed. See-through exposes the chute outlet, paddle faces, hub, direct axle and necessary supports. State in metadata and truth notes that this is the pictured waterwheel principle model, not a complete grain mill. Do not add a hopper, millstones, grain-feed action or gearing without further source evidence.

builderTruthNotes: Simple source diagram. Chute, paddles, hub, vertical axle and drawn supports are enough. Do not manufacture mill machinery to reach a label count.

Label all meaningful drawn real components and physical features. Distinguish force and travel overlays from anatomy. The individual builder brief must declare its expected minimum before building. No invented parts to meet a quota.

truthNotes: Pictured waterwheel principle model only, not a complete grain mill.
Supply tank, slide gate, catch tray, base and bearing supports are bench teaching fixtures.

Open water toggles the gate; Reduce flow toggles between illustrative 0.25 and 0.08 L/s inputs; Slow view toggles the whole explanatory clock between 1x and 0.25x; Reset represents manual refilling and emptying by a teacher.
Finite 5 L supply. Water accumulates in the catch tray and is not recirculated.
Rotor, hub and axle share one angle and speed. No gearing, hopper, millstone or grain action.
Speed response and flow values are qualitative teaching assumptions, not measured historical performance.
1988 remains inaccessible and unverified. No edition union claim.
